_comment: Measurement specification template for the round-2 certificate campaign. Targets and probes are referenced by role names or files; no real domains or addresses are written here. prereg.sha256 must be filled before submission; the budget script reads this file to produce the cost tiers.

prereg._axes_note: Amendment 1.1: o4 is promoted from optional to mandatory (only o4 can falsify c5); o1 is demoted to an optional axis, lit in the L1SP/L2S6 tiers that carry ping

defaults._interval_note: one round per hour, using the smallest recurring interval the platform permits
defaults._stagger_note: start times are staggered by >=60 s across measurements so that a serial server is not saturated concurrently (a round-1 anchor lesson)

sni._contrast_note: RFC 6761 reserved domain: it never resolves and is never issued, so it points at no third-party virtual host. It contributes only the second sni_map entry and never enters tls.hashes
sni.identity_name_rule: the domain on which the round-1 identity claim rested (the A-record name of the same explicit address); stored in the targets file, not in this template
sni._why_identity_required: c5 is a front end that selects certificates by name. If neither arm presents a real name it returns the same default certificate and the test loses its power (false negative)
never: write the two name conditions to different probes

probes._mode_note: an explicit prb_id array is required: a newly created user tag is not accepted by probe selection immediately (about a 15-minute lag), and all three measurement types must land on the same probes before their bundles can be merged

defaults._retire_note: never delete; stop only. The paper and the response letter cite the measurement IDs

arms.role: experimental arm: heterogeneous targets from S1, feeding the H1 statistic

measurements._target_kind_note: a domain target is rejected by the API's pre-resolution check; resolve it over DoH first, then target the address and present the name

arms.role: negative controls: the eight known single-certificate fleets of round 1, testing H2 specificity
positive control: round-1 target A (two known fingerprints, known re-signing)
controlled rotation rig (laboratory, known pool), testing H3/H4

measurements._o4_note: Fix of 2026-11-12: the rig arm was a single SNI-less arm, violating meta.prereg.axes_required=[o3,o4,o6], and was rejected by launcher gate 2. The rig is the known-answer calibration and must run the same two-name instrument as the main line; otherwise H3/H4 cannot calibrate o4.

arms.role: controlled re-signing rig (new: a TLS-inspecting proxy that preserves subject and validity and swaps the issuer)

measurements._o4_note: As rig_rotation: extended to two names on 2026-11-12 to satisfy axes_required. The re-signing rig's o4 positive control is H4's known answer.

arms.role: negative controls (o4-corrected): the eight round-1 single-certificate fleets under two names on the same address, testing H2
arms._why: The offline preflight of 2026-11-11 (data/c1/round2/preflight.json) shows that TLS+ping lifts kappa only to 0.5, where c5 still ties with c1/c8, so 8/8 remain indistinguishable. Only o4 can falsify c5, hence the same-address two-name arm. Deployability of o4 is documented in atlas_sni_evidence.json (hostname is read_only=false with help_text 'Server Name Indication (SNI) hostname').

measurements._bundle_note: this arm's handshakes feed tls.hashes; the o3/o6 calibers are identical to round 1
this arm contributes only the second sni_map entry and never enters tls.hashes; otherwise o6 would record name divergence as rotation in time
measurements._same_ip_note: both arms must target the same explicit address with the same prb_ids and starts >=60 s apart; hostname takes two real identity names (author decision pending)

arms.role: positive control (o4-corrected): round-1 target A under two names on the same address
o1 supplement for the control arms (9 targets): lifts kappa from 0.5 to 0.667; H2 does not depend on it
experimental arm (o4-corrected): heterogeneous targets under two names on the same address plus ping; the H1 statistic
arms._why: The preflight shows that o1 cannot separate {c1,c5,c8}; if heterogeneous targets ran TLS+ping only, H1's decidability would be structurally driven toward zero. o4 is the only discriminating axis, so the main line must carry the two-name arm.

measurements._bundle_note: identity name: handshakes feed tls.hashes; o3/o6 as in round 1
contrast name: feeds sni_map only, never tls.hashes
measurements._same_ip_note: both arms: same explicit address, same prb_ids, starts >=60 s apart

measurements._bundle_note: same probe set as the two sslcert arms, for build_merged_bundle

arms._count_note: Measured on 2026-11-12: after exclusion criteria 1-5 only two targets pass under both names (one strong, one weak), so the pre-registered H1 has n=2 and its caliber needs the author's decision.

arms.role: o5 add-on arm (3 targets x 12 rounds): shows o5 is obtainable; not part of the main criteria
S1 heterogeneity screen (pre-campaign): one-off, many vantages across three time bands

measurements._kind_note: the screen uses the same name condition as the campaign (explicit address plus identity name); otherwise 'screened' does not imply 'still handshakes in the campaign'. Domain targets are rejected by the API's pre-resolution check.

measurements._why: prereg §4 exclusion 5: test before the campaign whether the target rejects an unknown name outright; rejected targets do not enter the 48-hour window, saving window and credits

arms.role: vantage capability pre-test (D5 expanded): 9 control targets x 24 candidate probes x 2 names, one-off
arms._why: In round 1, 24 probes produced >=3 handshakes, each at exactly one target, so the intersection is empty (data/c1/round2/probe_seed.json). The whitelist cannot be inherited from round 1, and a rig-only pre-test cannot show that these probes handshake against third-party stacks. The campaign needs TLS and ping on the same probes, so the whitelist is the intersection of probes that qualify at all nine targets under both names.
arms._whitelist_rule: Take the intersection of probes that complete a handshake at all nine targets under both names; when the intersection is >=4 use it directly (4 per target, optionally 6). Below 4, backfill by descending number of qualifying targets, then descending handshakes at those targets, then ascending prb_id, and record the backfill and its reason in deviations.md.

arms.role: cross-round pilot for o1 heterogeneity (a screening extension, not part of any hypothesis test): whether a probe's TTL changes across 12 rounds
arms._why: a single-round screen cannot assess o1: the ttl of an echo reply is the remaining hop count, and cross-vantage differences are path-length differences. True heterogeneity is a same-probe TTL set of cardinality greater than one across rounds

measurements._note: four vantages drawn with area=WW over 12 rounds; the criterion reads each (target, probe) TTL set across them

ladder._comment: Three original tiers (L1/L2/L3) plus two o4-corrected tiers (L1S/L1SP). L1 tests G2 only; without passing L1, L2 must not start. The offline preflight of 2026-11-11 found that the TLS+ping combination of the original tiers cannot falsify c5, so H2 is structurally unreachable (8/8 remain indistinguishable); G2 must therefore be tested via L1S/L1SP. The original tiers are retained for audit only and must not be launched.

L1.description: 24 h, the nine existing targets (eight negative controls plus A), TLS+ping [original tier: preflight found H2 unreachable; do not use]

L1S.description: 24 h, nine targets x two names on the same address (o3/o4/o6, kappa=0.5) plus the vantage pre-test: the minimum deliverable for G2

L1SP.description: L1S plus the control-arm ping (o1/o3/o4/o6, kappa=0.667), which also leaves observations for H1's TTL heterogeneity criterion

L2.description: 48 h, eight controls plus 8-10 heterogeneous plus the positive control, TLS+ping
L2._void: No power for H1 (the L1 problem): the heterogeneous arm lacks o4. Retained for audit only; must not be launched.

L2S.description: 48 h, the o4-corrected main line: eight controls plus 8-10 heterogeneous plus the positive control, all under two names on the same address (plus ping on heterogeneous targets); two rigs for H3/H4
L2S._cost_note: Re-budgeted after D5: total 102,576, upper bound 108,912, stop line 10,891, so 113,467 must be pre-charged against a 113,573 baseline, leaving 106 and no buffer; not recommended. The selected tier is L2S6 (total 84,912, needs 93,806).

L2S6.description: L2S trims the heterogeneous arm to six targets (saving four targets x 48 h x two names plus ping): the only o4 main line that fits the balance
L2S6._note: Target trimming must share the control arms' window, otherwise H2 and H1 are not comparable; fewer heterogeneous targets only widens H1's Wilson interval
L2S6._cost_note: Selected tier (author decision, 2026-11-11): total 84,912, upper bound 88,944, stop line 8,894, so 93,806 must be pre-charged, leaving 19,767 against the 113,573 baseline. Includes the D5 pre-test (8,640) and the S1 screen (10,800).

L2Sc.description: L2S drops the 48-hour negative-control arm and reuses the 24-hour control results of L1S: cheaper, but the windows differ, so it serves as a sensitivity analysis only
L2Sc._caveat: prereg §8 states that targets with different window lengths are not pooled; this tier's H2 can only be reported for the L1S window and may not share a table with H1

L3.description: L2 plus the o5 add-on arm (3 targets x 12 rounds of traceroute)

PILOT_TTL.description: 24 candidates x 4 vantages x 12 rounds of recurring ping (3,456 credits): answers cheaply whether H1 has any targets at all

stop_rules.trigger: any target reached status 'Forced to Stop'
